failure_summary.description: Agents chose an adjacent endpoint instead of one matching the requested operation or source, such as a disposable-domain check for role-account classification or generic Arabic headlines for a named publisher.
The news request omitted distinct global and named-source results while adding a redundant general search for anime.
An optional language parameter was placed in the required-parameters slot.

patch.reasoning: The existing skill already covers action tracking and schema compliance, so repeating those broad rules is unwarranted. A focused clarification can help resolve the common endpoint-selection failure by treating named providers and sources as constraints and distinguishing adjacent operations and scopes.

edits.target: - Choose an endpoint by its documented operation, output, target, and support for the requested qualifiers—not merely by a shared topic or entity name. Prefer the most specific endpoint that fits the request; use separate endpoints when distinct deliverables require them.
edits.content: - When the user explicitly names a provider, endpoint, or source, treat that name as part of the target and choose the matching documented endpoint rather than a generic or neighboring one. Distinguish adjacent operations and scopes (for example, role-account classification from disposable-domain detection, or a named publisher's feed from general headlines in that language). Match each requested category to an endpoint with the corresponding output and scope; do not add an alternate search for a result already covered.
